# Results

**Generated by `benchmarks/build_results_page.py` from `load_testing/results/*.json`.** Every number below is a measurement; none was typed. Re-run the suite and this page regenerates.

```powershell
.\benchmarks\run_evidence_suite.ps1      # sections 1-4 and 6, ~50 min
.\benchmarks\ablate_long_prefill.ps1    # section 5a
.\benchmarks\ablate_gateway.ps1 ...     # section 5b (arguments in the script header)
python benchmarks/build_results_page.py
```

## What produced these numbers

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Engine | vLLM 0.11.0 (V1), `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-AWQ`, AWQ via the Marlin kernel |
| Context window | 32,768 tokens |
| Scheduler | `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, `--long-prefill-token-threshold 512`, `--max-num-seqs 32`, prefix caching on |
| Admission | 10 requests in flight, 12 queued with a 1.0 s timeout, per-key share up to 5 |
| Weighted cost | `1 + uncached_prompt_tokens / 2,048` slots, capped at 8; the cached part is estimated from the conversation's previous turn |
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop, 4,096 MiB, 35 W, thermally limited at 87 °C |
| Workload | Poisson arrivals, log-normal think time (mean 12 s), 6-message conversations that accumulate context, 192-token replies, seed 42, 120 s per run, heat-soaked first |
| Clients | Retry a `503` like the OpenAI SDK: two retries on `Retry-After`, then the person waits a think time and sends the same message again |
| SLO | First token within **1.5 s of the message's first send**, retries included |

### The metric

**SLO attainment** is the share of messages whose first token arrived within 1.5 s of the moment the user first pressed send. A message refused once has already missed it, because the retry comes at least 2 s later. This is the goodput framing used in serving research, and it is the user's view.

The column **TTFT p95, admitted** is the engine's view: latency of the requests the gateway let through. It is reported for comparison, never as the SLO: it cannot see refused messages, so judged by it alone, refusing everyone would score perfectly.

## 1. Capacity

| scenario | users | SLO attainment | served first try | never served | TTFT p50, user | TTFT p95, user | TTFT p95, admitted | users with every message on time | out tok/s | mean prompt | cache hit % | preempt |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| steady, 10 users | 10 | **100%** ✅ | 100% | 0 | 166.1 | 853.9 | 853.9 | 10/10 | 92 | 979 | 79 | 0 |
| steady, 20 users | 20 | **97%** ✅ | 97% | 0 | 243.3 | 1123.5 | 839.8 | 17/20 | 182 | 959 | 88 | 0 |
| steady, 25 users | 25 | **67%** ❌ | 71% | 1 | 1011.4 | 7839.6 | 1437.3 | 3/25 | 195 | 900 | 74 | 0 |
| steady, 25 users — repeat | 25 | **78%** ⚠️ | 81% | 3 | 657.7 | 14279.4 | 1315.2 | 7/25 | 184 | 872 | 93 | 0 |
| steady, 30 users | 30 | **64%** ❌ | 71% | 1 | 917.3 | 30520.9 | 1823.1 | 5/30 | 218 | 916 | 87 | 0 |
| steady, 40 users | 40 | **35%** ❌ | 41% | 13 | 4196.2 | 32755.2 | 1633.1 | 0/40 | 230 | 759 | 85 | 0 |
| steady, 60 users | 60 | **24%** ❌ | 27% | 38 | 7671.3 | 61025.3 | 2190.5 | 0/60 | 236 | 552 | 81 | 0 |
| **control** (10 users, re-run last) | 10 | **100%** ✅ | 100% | 0 | 303.1 | 891.8 | 891.8 | 10/10 | 91 | 931 | 81 | 0 |

**20 concurrent chat users with at least 9 in 10 messages starting within 1.5 s**, counting every refusal and retry. The knee is sharp: by 25 users the engine is saturated, and what gives is the share of messages served first time. Admitted p95 stays between 0.8 and 2.2 s at every level, because the queue timeout bounds the wait: requests that are served get a first token within about 2 s, never minutes.

**Past the knee, repeat runs disagree, and the disagreement is real.** 25 users gave 67% and 78%; 40 users gave 35% and 61% in independent runs with identical settings (the second 25-user run was added after the sweep; the second 40-user run is the matching arm of the admission ablation in section 5b). Refused users return 2–3 s later, so past saturation the offered load feeds on itself and small differences in timing or clock speed compound. Below the knee, the 10-user control reproduced exactly.

**The control makes the sweep comparable.** The 10-user level, re-run after everything else, gave 100% attainment against 100%. Starting cold instead of heat-soaked moved an identical run's throughput by 42% on this card, so every run is heat-soaked first and the control checks it stayed that way.

## 2. Traffic shapes a real service meets

| scenario | users | SLO attainment | served first try | never served | TTFT p50, user | TTFT p95, user | TTFT p95, admitted | users with every message on time | out tok/s | mean prompt | cache hit % | preempt |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| burst (4x spike mid-run) | 80 | **11%** ❌ | 24% | 51 | 9277.1 | 61683.3 | 2983.4 | 0/80 | 188 | 539 | 73 | 0 |
| thundering herd (all at once) | 60 | **9%** ❌ | 12% | 35 | 13514.3 | 82087.2 | 3230.2 | 0/60 | 202 | 615 | 63 | 0 |
| ramp (population grows) | 60 | **54%** ❌ | 54% | 26 | 1030.0 | 24787.7 | 1378.0 | 4/60 | 213 | 732 | 84 | 0 |
| diurnal (slow sine) | 40 | **87%** ⚠️ | 87% | 6 | 284.3 | 4833.3 | 1233.4 | 23/40 | 202 | 826 | 95 | 0 |

Spikes well past capacity fail on attainment, not on correctness: nothing errors, every refusal carries `Retry-After`, and admitted p95 stays between 1.2 and 3.2 s. The shapes that matter most in practice are the gentle ones: a slow daily cycle peaking at 40 users loses little, because the peak is brief and the cache stays warm.

## 3. Conversation length

| scenario | users | SLO attainment | served first try | never served | TTFT p50, user | TTFT p95, user | TTFT p95, admitted | users with every message on time | out tok/s | mean prompt | cache hit % | preempt |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ~300-token openings | 20 | **88%** ⚠️ | 92% | 0 | 401.0 | 3999.3 | 1494.3 | 8/20 | 181 | 588 | 82 | 0 |
| ~2,000-token openings | 20 | **60%** ❌ | 64% | 0 | 605.7 | 37953.7 | 2914.4 | 1/20 | 134 | 1808 | 74 | 0 |
| ~8,000-token openings | 20 | **27%** ❌ | 32% | 10 | 5144.9 | 82997.6 | 5350.2 | 0/20 | 51 | 6244 | 70 | 0 |

Every user in the long-conversation runs opens by pasting that much context, so each run starts with twenty cold prefills. That is a real capacity limit, not a gateway choice: prefill is quadratic, and twenty ~8k-token openings are close to a minute of GPU time on their own. Later turns are cheap, because the engine serves the history from the prefix cache and the gateway charges only the uncached part.

## 4. Fairness under an abusive client

| scenario | users | SLO attainment | served first try | never served | TTFT p50, user | TTFT p95, user | TTFT p95, admitted | users with every message on time | out tok/s | mean prompt | cache hit % | preempt |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10 normal users + 1 abusive key at 50 concurrent | 10 | **94%** ✅ | 94% | 0 | 511.8 | 3660.1 | 1165.1 | 7/10 | 89 | 887 | 83 | 0 |

The abusive key sent **2,079** requests and had **2,014 refused (96.9%)**. A key's share is `ceil(10 / contending keys)`, capped at 5, so one client can never hold more than half the engine, and less as soon as anyone else shows up.

> The attacker runs in a **separate process**. Sharing an event loop with the victims measured the simulator's own scheduling delay as server latency: a ~10x error, in the direction that makes a working mechanism look broken.

## 5. Ablations behind the shipped configuration

### 5a. Head-of-line blocking: `--long-prefill-token-threshold`

vLLM 0.11's V1 scheduler serves running requests first, and a long prompt mid-prefill takes the whole 2,048-token step, so everything that arrives behind a 20k-token prompt waits for all of it. The threshold caps one prefill's share of each step and the rest goes to new arrivals. A lower cap also splits every prompt longer than the cap into more steps, so ordinary traffic was measured alongside.

| threshold | 20k prompt TTFT | short requests behind it, worst TTFT | 20 users: SLO attainment | ~2k-token convs | ~8k-token convs |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 (vLLM default) | 13.3 s | **12,942 ms** | 87% | 78% | 26% |
| **512 — shipped** | 12.3 s | **378 ms** | 90% | 91% | 21% |
| 1024 | 12.1 s | **547 ms** | 97% | 84% | 29% |
| 0 (vLLM default) — control | 11.4 s | **11,116 ms** | 97% | 83% | 12% |

**Read the ordinary-traffic columns against the control.** The two threshold-0 runs, identical settings, gave 87% and 97% for 20-user chat. Every difference between thresholds in those columns sits inside that spread, so the one effect larger than the noise is head-of-line blocking, the second column.

The flag vLLM's docs pair with this one, `--max-num-partial-prefills > 1`, is what crash-loops this build (V0 fallback). The threshold alone is honoured by the V1 scheduler, and it is all that was needed.

### 5b. Tuning the gateway from the user's side

Both settings are scored on SLO attainment with retrying clients, because a refusal is a delay the user pays, not a free outcome.

**Queue timeout** (measured at 6 requests in flight):

| queue timeout | 20 users: SLO attainment | 40 users | admitted p95 at 40 users |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.6 s | 51% / 84% (control) | 35% | 1,159 ms |
| 1.0 s | 79% | 51% | 1,240 ms |
| 2.0 s | 81% | 36% | 2,058 ms |

The arithmetic bound `timeout ≈ SLO − engine TTFT` gives 0.6 s, but it treats a refusal as free. A refused client retries after `Retry-After: 2`, so it waits longer than a queued one would have. 1.0 s is shipped: best at 40 users, while 2.0 s pushed *admitted* p95 past the SLO. At 20 users the arms sit inside the run-to-run spread, which the two 0.6 s runs show plainly.

**Admission limit** (queue timeout 1.0 s):

| requests in flight | 20 users: SLO attainment | 40 users | admitted p95 at 40 users | output tok/s at 40 users |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6 | 85% / 92% (control) | 44% | 1,166 ms | 256 |
| 8 | 96% | 61% | 1,218 ms | 299 |
| 10 | 99% | 61% | 1,082 ms | 308 |

A ramp in which **every** request is a cold ~512-token prefill holds 6 inside the SLO. Chat resends its history, which the engine serves from the prefix cache, so each chat request is far cheaper and the engine holds 10 with *admitted* latency no worse than at 6. At 40 users 8 and 10 tie near 300 tok/s: that plateau is the GPU, and more slots past it would only add latency. Cold prompts are still charged by their uncached size, which keeps a burst of them out of the regime the ramp measured.

**How strong this evidence is.** The arms ran back to back in one heat-soaked session, and every pairing favoured the higher limit. But across all runs at the final configuration, 20-user attainment ranged from 87% to 97% (sections 1 and 5a), which overlaps the 85–92% measured at 6. The decision rests on the paired comparison, on admitted latency not getting worse, and on the reason for 6 not applying to chat, not on a gap larger than the noise.

## 6. Failure injection

| case | expected | measured | |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: |
| 1. Burst 10x over admission limit (100 simultaneous) | p95 TTFT bounded; excess refused with 503 + Retry-After, not queued | 12 served, 88 shed (Retry-After: 2); served p95 TTFT 1441.0 ms | ✅ |
| 3. Single ~20k-token prompt alongside normal traffic | short requests keep flowing; their TTFT rises but stays in low seconds | big prompt HTTP 200, 20448 tok, TTFT 18780.8 ms; small requests p95 TTFT 98.8 ms alone -> 636.1 ms during; 0 shed | ✅ |
| 4. Conversation outgrows the context window | 200 with oldest turns dropped and reported; never a hard 400 (window 32,768) | HTTP 200, X-Context-Trimmed-Messages=27, prompt sent ~95,488 tok -> engine saw 9726 tok | ✅ |
| 7. Client disconnects mid-stream | slot released within seconds, in-flight returns to 0, usage still recorded | in-flight 0 -> 0 after abandoning the stream at chunk 3; admitted_total 1723 | ✅ |
| 8. Slow client reading ~1 chunk/second | holds at most one slot; other users unaffected; bounded by stream timeout | 5/5 concurrent normal requests succeeded while the slow reader ran; their TTFT p50 127.0 ms; in-flight during test 1 | ✅ |
| 11. Budget exhausted mid-conversation | clean 429 with budget headers; conversation resumable on a funded key | 429 after 0 served requests; X-Budget-Remaining=0; same conversation on a funded key -> HTTP 200 | ✅ |
| 12. Billing ledger unwritable (disk full / permissions) | bounded unbilled requests, then 503 (fail CLOSED), then automatic recovery | [200, 200, 200, 503, 503, 503] while unwritable -> 3 served unbilled before the breaker tripped; HTTP 503 during cooldown; HTTP 200 after cooldown | ✅ |
| 10. KV pressure / preemption with exact accounting | every served request bills exactly 700 completion tokens; zero drift | 3 served, 9 shed; ledger +12 rows, +2100 completion tokens (expected 2100); engine preemptions +0 | ✅ |

**8 of 8 pass.**

**Process failures under load** (`load_testing/kill_test.py`):

| event | recovery | requests during the event | accounting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| engine core crashes mid-generation | back in **79.4 s** (restart policy); gateway `/health` stayed 200, `/ready` went 200/503 | {'200': 4, '500': 3, '502': 149} | 156 rows for 156 requests, drift **0** |
| gateway restarted | back in **4.8 s** | {'200': 4, 'RemoteProtocolError': 5} | budgets survived: **yes** |

The gateway staying live (`/health` 200) while reporting not-ready (`/ready` 503) is the point of the split: its upstream died, it did not, and restarting it would only drop the requests that were about to succeed.

Full matrix with reasoning: [FAILURE_MATRIX.md](FAILURE_MATRIX.md).
